Alex.confusing: How hugs interact with visitors: I assumed only a Floofer's own visitors get hugged, so I wrongly read Casey as the Floofer in round 3.
Alex.fun: Round 2 as Mouser: claiming the safe Eagle and watching the table pile onto Finley, with my doubled 11 banking.
Alex.change: Make the bonus scoring clearer, since the doubled Meowfia banks dominated the final standings and decided who won.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I accused Casey outright on a hug inference and staked my 7 and 6 on it. I should have staked low cards and kept the high ones, since the vote was a 3-3 tie and my read was wrong.

Blair.confusing: How hugs and confusion interact with visitor reports, e.g. whether a Kookaburra's "confused" status could explain the hug claims and egg counts in round 2.
Blair.fun: Round 1, when my Hawk egg confirmed Drew as Meowfia and the table piled on him. The 27-point banked throw was a great payoff.
Blair.change: I'd show Farm players a little more verifiable information, since Meowfia could invent claims too easily. I'd also soften the swing from big stakes that get discarded after a wrong read.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I threw H13 and C6 at Finley on a read that mostly rested on Casey's unverified hug claim. I should have kept my big cards, since my own Owl report only showed Hawk and Tit visiting Finley and nothing pointed to Finley being Meowfia.

Casey.confusing: How hugs, confusion and visitor lists interact. In round 2 I couldn't tell whether my hug proved Finley was the Floofer, since a Floofer's hug extends to anyone who visits them. Neither could I tell whether Finley's "confused" claim could be true.
Casey.fun: Round 1: the Eagle gave me hard evidence, Alex and Blair's visits to Drew. That let me throw my 13, 12 and 10 with confidence, and the stake banked for 35 points.
Casey.change: Add a way to verify claims, or limit how much a throw reveals. As it stands, a confident bluff can cost a whole table the round, as in round 2, when everyone piled onto a Farm player.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I treated the hug as proof that Finley was Meowfia and threw 13, 8 and 7 at him. Drew, the real Floofer, had also been named as suspicious. I should have thrown lower cards or hedged, and weighed the Meowfia's incentive to fake a hug story. In round 3 I should have kept my high cards.

Drew.confusing: How the Floofer's hug interacts with other roles' reports and the Kookaburra's confusion, since players kept citing it to prove or disprove each other's stories.
Drew.fun: Round 2, when the whole table threw at Finley, a Farm player, and my Meowfia stake doubled for a big score jump.
Drew.change: Show the exact stake and banking math at throw time. A Farm player's stake banks even when the eggsecuted player is someone else, and that was easy to lose track of.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I winked Casey, which made me look guilty and got me eggsecuted. In round 3 I threw 26 points of cards at Alex on a shaky read, and I would have thrown fewer high cards.

Ellis.confusing: How the scoring bonus works. The final scores showed large "bonus" numbers that I couldn't match to the rules text, and the "Grudge" doubling wasn't explained either.
Ellis.fun: Round 1, where I caught Finley's false claim of visiting my Turkey. Round 3 was also fun: I played Floofer, claimed Hawk, and steered the vote onto Casey.
Ellis.change: I'd show more public information about how scores build up. Meowfia with a Wink also decided too much, since the round-2 Mouser and Floofer pair was hard for Farm to see through.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I threw 3 big cards (H10, D7, D5) at Finley on a consensus read, and he was Farm, so I lost most of my nest. I should have thrown 1 or 2 low cards and kept my high ones, because the vote was already lopsided and my stake didn't change it.

Finley.confusing: The Grudge doubling in the final round. It was not in the rules I was given, and the scoring was unclear about when it applies and how the bonus is counted.
Finley.fun: Round 3, when I was Meowfia and my partner and I both threw at Casey. I banked three high cards, and the table's argument over the Falcon hug and the Kookaburra's lost egg was fun to watch.
Finley.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer when a player is confused. Right now a confused player can't separate a bad report from a good one, and that makes the day's deduction very noisy.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I claimed Falcon and said I visited Ellis, which was a sloppy lie. It drew suspicion to me and cost the round. I should have picked a claim and visit that fit the egg counts, and kept quiet instead of hinting at doubt.

review.title: Wild Stakes, Quiet Cats
review.headline: Finley lost one round, won two quietly, and took the whole game.
review.summary: Round 1 was a clean Farm win: Drew's Wink on Casey backfired and the table threw high at him. Round 2 flipped it. Alex and Drew, both Meowfia, sat back while the table piled onto Farm Finley after Casey's hug evidence, and the cats banked huge. In round 3 the Meowfia pair Ellis and Finley steered the vote onto Farm Casey. Finley ended first on 84 with a lot of double-value stakes.

rounds.recap: Alex, Blair and Casey all visited Drew, and Drew winked Casey after he named Drew's visitors. The Wink only made Drew look worse. Everyone threw high at Drew and Farm won big. Finley's Falcon claim was visibly false.

Drew hugged Casey, and Casey correctly reasoned that a Floofer was involved. Casey then pointed at Finley, a confused Farm Kookaburra, and the table followed. Both cats threw big at Finley, who was eggsecuted as Farm. Meowfia banked doubled stakes: Drew jumped from 5 to 73.

Ellis (Floofer) hugged Alex, so Alex's true Falcon claim sounded like a lie. Alex blamed Casey and the table split between Alex and Casey. The cats threw together at Casey. Finley's 8-card nest let him stake three high cards and win the game.

highlights.text: Drew winks Casey right after Casey names the visitors, which proves nothing but makes Drew look guilty.
Casey's hug logic is sound, but it points at the wrong person: confusion and hugs together create a false Floofer suspect.
Blair, an honest Owl, catches Drew's false Falcon claim, yet the table still convicts Finley.
Ellis hugs Alex, then uses Alex's honest hug claim as proof he is lying, and the Meowfia pair slips through.

confusions.what: Claimed Falcon visited Ellis and expected an egg from a Turkey, then muddled it mid-message.
Said Casey's +2 fits two visitors, and Drew's Kookaburra claim was judged confused by the table without a clear rule check.
Argued a Kookaburra would be confused by visitors, but his own claim then contradicted the visits he knew about.
Garbled his Eagle report about the +2 and was unsure where his eggs came from.
Claimed Eagle and said he saw no other visitor to Casey, a claim that could not be true for a Mouser.
Treated his confused report as a real loss, although confusion changes the report and not the nest.
Said Alex's hug claim conflicted with Casey's confusion, though the two were unrelated.

worked: Hug and Confused interactions: a Floofer visit leaves a believable false trail, and round 3 turned on it.
Owl and Eagle visitor reports gave real cross-checks, such as Blair catching Drew's false Falcon claim.
Doubled Meowfia stakes made correct framing very rewarding, so round 2 and 3 swung hard.
Egg count changes in the day listing gave players something concrete to argue about.
problems: Meowfia stakes are doubled and nests keep growing, so the cat who frames a Farm player gains huge points (Drew 5 to 73). Cap the multiplier or the throw size.
Round 1 showed a Wink is weak: it looked guilty and gave nothing. Consider hiding the death cause better or giving it a clearer upside.
Scores swing so much that round 3 had little tension about the winner. Rubber-band the point values or reduce the 5-point round bonus.
Many players visited at random and had no useful way to choose, so early nights were noise. A first-night hint could help.
Confused reports are hard to track: players mixed up whether the nest or just the report was wrong. Rewrite that text for clarity.
